public_rationale: The ordinary business-model comparison holds. Uber operates transport, delivery and freight marketplaces. Anthropic and OpenAI supply access to generative models through applications, paid plans and APIs. This supports a material difference in their core businesses. It does not establish that all economic comparisons are invalid: Uber's own report describes memberships and activity-related costs.
limitations: The result depends on reading completely different as materially different in core business.
The evidence directly covers the two named AI providers, not every business that might be called an AI company.
This assessment does not validate the separate assertions about Uber's assets or the causes of its losses.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Uber is a completely different business from Anthropic, OpenAI, or any other AI company.

statement.excerpt: Uber is a completely different business to Anthropic and OpenAI or any other AI company.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: Uber is a completely different business
our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading is that Uber's core service and commercial model differ materially from businesses developing and selling access to generative models.
Completely different is treated as an emphatic business-model comparison, not a claim that the companies share no costs, technology or commercial practices.
Any other AI company is read within the surrounding discussion of generative model providers. It is not extended to every company using AI.
I use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual operating period reportable before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Primary descriptions show that Uber principally connects participants in transport, delivery and freight markets, while the named AI providers sell access to their models and applications through paid plans and APIs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Primary descriptions show that Uber and the named providers principally supply the same service through substantially the same commercial model.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business: Overview and Our Segments; also Membership and Item 7 cost-of-revenue discussion
evidence.explanation: Uber describes connecting riders, merchants, couriers, shippers and carriers. The report also identifies Uber One memberships and service costs that vary with activity, limiting any stronger interpretation that Uber shares no commercial features or variable costs with AI providers.

evidence.locator: Opening announcement, paragraph describing Claude plans and model availability
evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes access to its own models through Claude plans, its API and cloud platforms. This differs materially from Uber's transport and delivery marketplace.

evidence.locator: Opening section, paragraph immediately before Model performance
evidence.explanation: OpenAI describes distributing its models through paid ChatGPT plans and developer APIs. Together with Uber's filing, this supports the ordinary comparison of their core businesses.
